{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Das Fotoalbum für Weierstraß 025 (Johann Gustav Hermes).jpg|thumb|Johann Gustav Hermes ]]
'''Johann Gustav Hermes''' (20 June 1846 – 8 June 1912) was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]]. Hermes is known for constructing a [[65,537-gon|polygon with 65,537 sides]].

== Early life ==
On 20 June 1846, Hermes was born in [[Königsberg]], a former German city (presently [[Kaliningrad]], Russia). Hermes was educated at the Kneiphöfischen [[Gymnasium (school)|Gymnasium]].  He undertook his ''Abitur'' (final examination) at the school in 1866.  After completing his secondary education, he studied [[mathematics]] from 1866 to 1870, mostly in [[Königsberg]]. His studies were interrupted due to his participation in the [[Franco-Prussian War]] between 1870 and 1871.

== Education ==
On 14 December 1872, Hermes completed his studies and earned a degree in mathematics. 
On 5 April 1879, Hermes received a [[doctorate]] degree and his [[Thesis|dissertation]] was on the "Reduction of the problem of [[cyclotomy]] on linear equations (for [[prime number]]s of the form 2<sup>''m''</sup>+1)" (German: "''Zurückführung des Problems der Kreistheilung auf lineare Gleichungen (für Primzahlen von der Form'' 2<sup>''m''</sup>+1'')''").<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=59625 |title=Mathematics Genealogy Project - Johann Gustav Hermes |publisher=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |access-date=December 28, 2018}}</ref>

== Career ==
After a probationary year at the [[Chernyakhovsk]] Realgymnasium in 1873, Hermes worked as a teacher at the Progymnasium of the Royal Orphanage of Königsberg in Prussia (German: ''Königliches Waisenhaus zu Königsberg in Preußen''). Beginning in 1883 he was an ''Oberlehrer'' (or upper teacher). In 1893 he became a professor at the Georgianum Gymnasium in [[Lingen]]. Finally, on 1 April 1899, he became a professor and director at the [[Osnabrück]] Realgymnasium (now named the Ernst-Moritz-Arndt-Gymnasium). 

On 31 December 1906 he asked for an early retirement from his position due to illness. 

=== Achievements ===
In 1894, Hermes completed his decade-long effort to find and write down a procedure for the [[Compass and straightedge constructions|construction]] of the [[regular polygon|regular]] [[65537-gon]] exclusively with a compass and a straightedge. His manuscript, with over 200 pages, is today located at the [[University of Göttingen]].

In his maiden speech as the director at the Osnabrück Realgymnasium on 11 April 1899, he praised the [[Categorical imperative|concept of duty]] of the influential [[Philosophy|philosopher]] [[Immanuel Kant]], who was also a resident of Königsberg. He finished with the words "''Geduld ist die Pforte der Freude.''" ("Patience is the gate to joy.")

== Personal life ==
Hermes became ill in December 1906, and died on 8 June 1912. He is buried in Osnabrück, Germany.
